## What a rolling mean does {#smooth data-hold="true"}

```{=html}
<div class="bridgew" id="rollw">
  <div class="sm-controls">
    <label class="sm-slider">Window <strong id="rw-label">6 h</strong>
      <input type="range" id="rw-len" min="1" max="24" step="1" value="6">
    </label>
    <div class="sm-mode" role="group" aria-label="Window position">
      <button type="button" data-a="trail" aria-pressed="true">Trailing</button>
      <button type="button" data-a="centre" aria-pressed="false">Centered</button>
    </div>
  </div>
  <svg id="rw-plot" viewBox="0 0 1160 300" role="img" aria-label="Four days of real benzene with a rolling mean drawn over it; the window and its position can be changed"></svg>
  <div class="sm-readout" id="rw-out" aria-live="polite"></div>
</div>
<script>
(function () {
  const root = document.getElementById('rollw'); if (!root) return;
  root.addEventListener('click', (e) => e.stopPropagation());
  // Real benzene, µg/m³, 27 to 30 April 2004 (Lab 03, Demo A, faults removed).
  const Y = [2.2,1.7,1.6,1.5,2.5,3.3,8.9,23.4,23.8,7.9,8.2,8.8,14.6,18,12,14.8,12.5,15.5,17.7,21.6,18.9,12.5,8.8,10.9,8,4.4,2.8,2.7,2.2,2.5,7.5,30.4,22,24.7,18.4,16.8,14.2,15.7,21.9,20.8,16.2,19.8,28.9,28.3,24.9,13.1,8.6,9.5,7.8,5.2,2.8,2.3,2.5,4.4,9.4,29.8,36.2,18,10.9,9,14.4,22.3,20.9,23.1,21.2,24.8,28.6,32.6,19.2,16.3,13.7,13.6,11.1,7.6,5.9,5,4,4.5,9.3,18.3,19.9,16.6,12.6,12.9,14.9,17.4,15.4,16.7,18,19.2,21,26.9,19.5,15.1,14.6,13.7];
  let align = 'trail';
  const N = Y.length, W = 1160, H = 300, L = 64, R = 16, T = 14, B = 44, top = 40;
  const X = (k) => L + (k / (N - 1)) * (W - L - R), V = (v) => T + (1 - v / top) * (H - T - B);
  const mean = (a) => a.reduce((s, v) => s + v, 0) / a.length;
  function roll(w) {   // as pandas rolling(w).mean() and rolling(w, center=True).mean()
    return Y.map((_, i) => { const a = align === 'trail' ? i - w + 1 : i - Math.floor(w / 2), b = a + w - 1; return a >= 0 && b < N ? mean(Y.slice(a, b + 1)) : null; });
  }
  function draw() {
    const w = +document.getElementById('rw-len').value, S = roll(w);
    document.getElementById('rw-label').textContent = w + ' h';
    let g = '';
    for (const v of [0, 10, 20, 30, 40]) g += `<line x1="${L}" x2="${W - R}" y1="${V(v)}" y2="${V(v)}" stroke="#B9C1C6"/><text x="${L - 10}" y="${V(v) + 6}" text-anchor="end" font-size="17" fill="#333F4A">${v}</text>`;
    for (let d = 0; d < 4; d++) g += `<line x1="${X(d * 24)}" x2="${X(d * 24)}" y1="${H - B}" y2="${H - B + 6}" stroke="#333F4A"/><text x="${X(d * 24 + 12)}" y="${H - 14}" text-anchor="middle" font-size="17" fill="#333F4A">${27 + d} April</text>`;
    g += `<text transform="translate(18 ${(T + H - B) / 2}) rotate(-90)" text-anchor="middle" font-size="16" fill="#66727C">benzene, µg/m³</text>`;
    g += `<line x1="${L}" x2="${L}" y1="${T}" y2="${H - B}" stroke="#333F4A" stroke-width="1.5"/><line x1="${L}" x2="${W - R}" y1="${H - B}" y2="${H - B}" stroke="#333F4A" stroke-width="1.5"/>`;
    g += `<path d="${Y.map((v, k) => (k ? 'L' : 'M') + X(k).toFixed(1) + ',' + V(v).toFixed(1)).join('')}" fill="none" stroke="#0F6E6B" stroke-width="1.8"/>`;
    let d = '', pen = false;
    S.forEach((v, k) => { if (v === null) { pen = false; return; } d += (pen ? 'L' : 'M') + X(k).toFixed(1) + ',' + V(v).toFixed(1); pen = true; });
    g += `<path d="${d}" fill="none" stroke="#E29A2D" stroke-width="3.5"/>`;
    // the 29 April morning peak: hour 56 (08:00) in the record
    let best = -1, at = -1;
    for (let k = 48; k < 72; k++) if (S[k] !== null && S[k] > best) { best = S[k]; at = k; }
    g += `<circle cx="${X(56)}" cy="${V(Y[56])}" r="6" fill="#0F6E6B"/>`;
    document.getElementById('rw-plot').innerHTML = g;
    const lag = align === 'trail' ? (w - 1) / 2 : (w % 2 ? 0 : 0.5);
    document.getElementById('rw-out').innerHTML = `<span class="sm-key"><i class="k-true"></i>record <i class="k-rec"></i>${w} h ${align === 'trail' ? 'trailing' : 'centered'} mean</span>` +
      `<span class="sm-chip">highest hour on 29 April: record <b>${Y[56].toFixed(1)}</b>, smoothed <b>${best.toFixed(1)}</b></span>` +
      `<span class="sm-chip ${lag >= 3 ? 'missed' : lag >= 1 ? 'blurred' : 'seen'}">the smoothed line runs <b>${lag.toFixed(1)} h</b> late</span>`;
  }
  document.getElementById('rw-len').addEventListener('input', draw);
  root.querySelectorAll('[data-a]').forEach((b) => b.addEventListener('click', () => { align = b.dataset.a; root.querySelectorAll('[data-a]').forEach((o) => o.setAttribute('aria-pressed', o === b)); draw(); }));
  draw();
})();
</script>
```

[Real benzene, 27 to 30 April 2004 (Lab 03, Demo A). Data: De Vito, UCI Air Quality, doi:10.24432/C59K5F, CC BY 4.0.]{.source}

## Two effects you cannot avoid {#effects}

::: {.beforeafter}
::: {}
[Peaks get lower]{.label}
A mean of w hours cannot be higher than the highest of them. In the Lab 03 demo, with the typical daily peak taken as the mean of the 14 daily maxima, a 6-hour mean lowers the typical daily peak from 21.5 to 16.1 µg/m³ (−25 %), and a 24-hour mean to 11.5 (−46 %).
:::
::: {}
[A trailing mean runs late]{.label}
It uses only past hours, so it lags by (w − 1)/2 hours: 2.5 hours for a 6-hour mean, 5.5 for 12. A centered mean removes most of the lag but needs future hours, so a live display cannot use it.
:::
:::

[Neither is a mistake. Both are mistakes if the chart does not say which mean it shows.]{.note-line}

## Activity 1 · The AI deletes outliers {#act1 .activity}

[Pairs · 10 minutes · Lab 03, Step 4]{.act-label}

```{=html}
<pre class="code-slide"><span>z = (df["C6H6_ugm3"] - df["C6H6_ugm3"].mean()) / df["C6H6_ugm3"].std()</span><span>df = df[z.abs() &lt; 3]                 <b class="c"># remove outliers</b></span><span>print(len(df), df["C6H6_ugm3"].mean())</span></pre>
```

::: {.prompt .small}
Name three things this code does to your file that the printed numbers do not show. Then say what you would do instead.
:::

::: {.selfstudy}
Studying alone: write your three things, then go on.
:::

## What it did {#act1-fix}

::: {.why3}
::: {.w}
[1 · Deleted real events]{.label}
**Rush hours above the mean + 3σ are removed.** They are the hours a benzene report is about.
:::
::: {.w}
[2 · Kept faults]{.label}
**A drop to 0.1 at noon stays in.** It is unusual for that hour, not for the record.
:::
::: {.w .hard}
[3 · Made gaps]{.label}
**Whole rows go**, so the series is no longer hourly, and the sensor value at those hours is lost too.
:::
:::

```{=html}
<pre class="code-slide"><span>s = df["C6H6_ugm3"]</span><span>med = s.rolling(7, center=True).median()</span><span>mad = s.rolling(7, center=True).apply(lambda w: np.median(np.abs(w - np.median(w))))</span><span>df["suspect"] = (s - med).abs() &gt; 3 * 1.4826 * mad   <b class="c"># Hampel: flag, do not delete</b></span></pre>
```

[Flag, then check each flagged hour against the second sensor. Remove only what you can show is a fault, and report it.]{.note-line}

## Rules for honest smoothing {#rules}

::: {.checks4}
::: {.c4}
[Say it]{.label}
Write the window and the position on the chart: "6-hour centered mean".
:::
::: {.c4}
[Keep the raw]{.label}
Draw the raw record lightly behind the smoothed line, so peaks stay visible.
:::
::: {.c4}
[Raw for limits]{.label}
Compare peaks with a limit, and time events, on the raw record, never on the smoothed one.
:::
::: {.c4}
[Fit the use]{.label}
Trailing for a live display, centered for a report written afterwards.
:::
:::

[Smoothing is for the reader's eye. It is not a way to remove values you do not like.]{.note-line}
